title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to probably website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the probably website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Refactor the estimation code for beta calibration
description:
Also incorporates changes for 1-vs-all calibration that will be relevant for isotonic methods. 

Some notes about the `estimates` elements of the calibration objects.  `estimates` should have two elements: 

 - `filter` should have 1 expression or null
 - `estimate` should be a list
    - if binary, a single element named after the first class level probability column
    - if multinomial or 1-vs-all, an element for each class named for the corresponding probability column 

It's unfortunate that the word "estimate" is used in a variety of different contexts

title: Refactor the estimation code for multinomial models
description:
The idea is to use tidyeval much earlier than the current code. This makes the code a lot less complex and readable. I've disabled some tests (like the validation functions) because we will have to modify those after all of the estimation methods are done. 

After this, the next steps are: 

- refactor regression
- refactor logistic
- refactor beta calibration
- refactor isotonic methods
- more testing with allowing 2+ grouping columns (in advance of censored regression)
- check for zero-variance groups and eliminate them
- update `cal_validate_*()`
- add checks for model failures and add fallback methods (if any)
- update the `required_pkgs()` methods to require nnet or mgcv when applicable.

Each of these will be at least one PR each.

title: convert expressions for levels
description:
Related to #145

The calibration objects store factor levels as expressions and we are seeing errors when subsetting columns or setting class levels in new factors: 

``` r
library(probably)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'probably'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     as.factor, as.ordered
data(two_class_example, package = "modeldata")
w_calibration <- cal_estimate_logistic(two_class_example,
                                       truth = truth,
                                       estimate = c(Class1, Class2))

cal_apply(two_class_example, w_calibration, pred_class = Class)
#> Error in `purrr::map()`:
#> ℹ In index: 1.
#> Caused by error in `[<-.data.frame`:
#> ! anyNA() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'symbol'
```

<sup>Created on 2024-09-20 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: Conformal prediction intervals
description:
Produces prediction intervals based on [https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116) (algorithm 1): 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5731043/217340494-d93505f3-4de5-4de1-8427-fba7eb86d40b.png)

The default for finding the intervals uses a fast root finding approach rather than grid search (there is an option to do that though). This method is 2-5-fold faster and seems to have acceptable properties (simulations to check coverage are forthcoming).

Currrently only implemented for regression models

title: better message for estimation functions when the levels are incomplete or incorrect
description:
Closes #94 

Different error messages: 

``` r
library(tidymodels)
library(probably)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'probably'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     as.factor, as.ordered
```

``` r

tidymodels_prefer()
theme_set(theme_bw())
options(pillar.advice = FALSE, pillar.min_title_chars = Inf)
```

``` r

# Previously, these both gave errors of '! Multiclass not supported...yet'

# The estimate function didn't specify all prediction columns: 
segment_logistic %>% cal_estimate_logistic(truth = Class, estimate = .pred_poor)
#> Error in `check_level_consistency()`:
#> ! We can't connect the specified prediction columns to some factor levels (good). The selected columns were .pred_poor. Are there more columns to add in the funciton call?
#> Backtrace:
#>     ▆
#>  1. ├─segment_logistic %>% ...
#>  2. ├─probably::cal_estimate_logistic(., truth = Class, estimate = .pred_poor)
#>  3. └─probably:::cal_estimate_logistic.data.frame(...)
#>  4.   └─probably:::cal_logistic_impl(...)
#>  5.     └─probably:::truth_estimate_map(...)
#>  6.       └─probably:::check_level_consistency(truth_levels, est_map)
#>  7.         └─rlang::abort(msg)

# (Incomplete specification of the columns _does_ work with the plot funcitons tho)

# Added better error for logistic with 3+ classes
hpc_cv %>% cal_estimate_logistic(truth = obs, estimate = c(VF:L))
#> Error in `cal_logistic_impl()`:
#> ! The number of outcome factor levels isn't consistent with the calibration method. The levels were: 'VF', 'F', 'M', 'L'
#> Backtrace:
#>     ▆
#>  1. ├─hpc_cv %>% ...
#>  2. ├─probably::cal_estimate_logistic(., truth = obs, estimate = c(VF:L))
#>  3. └─probably:::cal_estimate_logistic.data.frame(., truth = obs, estimate = c(VF:L))
#>  4.   └─probably:::cal_logistic_impl(...)
#>  5.     └─rlang::abort(msg)
```

<sup>Created on 2023-05-05 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

I've also updated the docs to say when we extend binary methods to multiclass.

description:
Related to #75 

Modifications: 

* Some error messages were changed since they assumed the outcome was a factor.
* `truth_estimate_map()` was updated to return a structure consistent with classification data when regression data are used.
* The code to check which metrics were used was expanded and refactored into a separate function. 
* The printing code was refactored with sub-functions for printing classification or regression objects.
* Some existing functions had name changes (e.g., adding `_cls`) so that we can differentiate the different types of models. 
* Many roxygen comments were edited or added to prep for different methods. A `man-roxygen` directory was added and included a few templates. 

No regression calibration tools were added here. Those will come in subsequent PRs. One will be for linear regression (completely analogous to the logistic code), and another will expand the isotonic regression tools for regression calibration.

title: Specify metrics in threshold_perf()
description:
## Description

So that the user can specify which metrics are computed when calling threshold_perf(), we add a new `metrics` argument that accepts a `yardstick` metric set.

By default this argument is `NULL`, in which case the function computes the default metrics. If not `NULL`, the function checks that it's an appropriate metric set (class metrics only) and computes only the metrics provided in the set.

## Motivation and Context

Fixes #25 

## How Has This Been Tested?

Tested using yardstick 0.0.7 on R 4.0.2.

## Types of changes
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

## Checklist:
- [ ] My code follows the [code style](https://style.tidyverse.org/) of this project.
- [x] My change requires a change to the documentation.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly.

Note that I did *not* add an example in the docs of `threshold_perf()` that uses the new feature.

title: Implement `event_level` argument for `threshold_perf()`
description:
Closes #40 

Not adding anything to `make_two_class_pred()`. The docs there are clear that `estimate` maps to the first level supplied in `levels` and I don't see any reason to support `event_level` there.

But `threshold_perf()` does need to support it because it computes metrics internally.

Since probably isn't used that much, and `event_level = "second"` is used even less, I've done a hard break by removing support for `yardstick.event_level` altogether in favor of the explicit `event_level` argument.

This PR modifies `make_class_pred()` and `two_class_pred()`.

There are now:

`make_class_pred()` and `make_two_class_pred()` which take vectors and return a vector that is a `class_pred` object.

`append_class_pred()` which takes in a data frame, and allows the user to specify the class prob columns with tidyselect helpers through the `...` argument.

There is no `append_two_class_pred()` because it is not useful since only 1 prob column is required.
